## Casebook (judgment layer)
> 6 case(s), 6 lesson(s) — worked studies + reusable lessons; retrieve by data fingerprint. See [SCHEMA.md](casebook/SCHEMA.md).
- [A million-count black-hole binary — where the error bars stop meaning what they say](casebook/cases/chandra-bhxrb-vhigh-systematics-001.md) (core)
- [Cluster metallicity on Chandra — how a single temperature biases the iron abundance threefold](casebook/cases/chandra-cluster-fe-bias-001.md) (core)
- [Faint GRB afterglow at low counts — cstat over chi, and freezing what the data cannot constrain](casebook/cases/chandra-grb-afterglow-001.md) (core)
- [Obscured Seyfert on Chandra — why an unabsorbed fit drives the photon index flat](casebook/cases/chandra-obscured-agn-001.md) (core)
- [Low-count NICER quiescent neutron star — cstat, and why bbodyrad is the wrong model](casebook/cases/nicer-lowcount-thermal-001.md) (core)
- [XRISM/Resolve cluster turbulence — 27000 counts, ~1 per bin, and why chi is still wrong](casebook/cases/xrism-cluster-turbulence-001.md) (core)

### Lessons
- [The statistic is set by counts per bin, not total counts: a high-resolution spectrum with tens of thousands of counts but ~1 per fine bin still needs cstat, not chi.](casebook/lessons/counts-per-bin-not-total-drives-statistic.md) (validated)
- [Use cstat, not chi, below ~1000 total counts on Poisson data.](casebook/lessons/cstat-below-1k-counts.md) (validated)
- [A power-law fit that drives the photon index implausibly flat (Gamma < ~1) is usually signalling missing low-energy absorption, not a hard intrinsic spectrum.](casebook/lessons/flat-photon-index-means-absorption.md) (validated)
- [A parameter pegged at a limit plus correlated residuals means the model is structurally wrong, not just badly initialised.](casebook/lessons/peg-at-limit-means-wrong-model.md) (validated)
- [Fitting a single-temperature plasma to multi-phase cluster/group gas biases the measured metallicity (usually low -- the 'Fe bias'); an elevated fit statistic is the tell.](casebook/lessons/single-temperature-fe-bias.md) (validated)
- [Above ~10^5 counts the statistical error bars shrink below the ~1-2% calibration floor, so they no longer represent the real uncertainty -- you are systematics-limited, and a reduced statistic above 1 usually flags an unmodelled few-percent feature.](casebook/lessons/systematics-dominate-above-1e5-counts.md) (candidate)
